observations: The page number «68» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01 continues the computation of p. 67 (JP2 0099, L41-L48): «Wahre Länge» is the true longitude of the moon, 332° 4′ (L41), «Länge des Drachenkopfes» the sum of the right column, 289° 51′ 57″ (L48). L33-L34: the heading of chapter 23, in bold, centred, with the reference to the text below it; L34 «58a», L05, L24 and L30 «57a», L29 «57b», the letters raised; L07 «11s», the s raised.

L01-L04. Checked: 332° 4′ − 289° 51′ 57″ = 42° 12′ 3″; 4° 30′ × sin 42° 12′ = 3° 1′ 21″ (Table 22: 3° 1′ 22″); 9° 37′ + 3° 1′ 22″ = 12° 38′ 22″, «rund 12° 38′»; 332° 4′ is 11 signs 2° 4′, in Pisces. L03: «(9° 37″)», the difference of p. 67 (L39) with the sign of the seconds; see the critical note.

L01. Checked: here the sum of Tables 19 and 20 is taken away from the true longitude of the moon as the longitude of the node. On p. 55 (JP2 0087, L10-L13) Suter explains that this sum is taken away from 360° to give the longitude of the node, since the node moves backwards, and on p. 59 (JP2 0091, L10-L32) he adds the sum to the true longitude (chapter 16 of the text, as he gives it on p. 58, JP2 0090, L33-L34), or takes 360° less the sum away from it. Counted that way, the node stands at 360° − 289° 51′ 57″ = 70° 8′, and the argument of latitude is 332° 4′ − 70° 8′ = 261° 56′, not 42° 12′; then the latitude is about 4° 27′ south (4° 30′ × sin 81° 56′), the distantia definita by the rule of the text (p. 66, JP2 0098, L35-L36: a southern latitude is subtracted) about 9° 37′ − 4° 27′ = 5° 10′, less than the 9° 21′ of Table 57a, and by L13-L16 the crescent would not be visible that evening. The modern mean node agrees with the reading of pp. 55 and 59: for 6 August 1145 (15 Ṣafar 540) and 14 February 1146 it is at 89.7° and 79.5° of the tropical ecliptic, about 9½° more than the 80° 19′ of p. 59 and the 70° 8′ found here, the difference that p. 42 (JP2 0074) finds between al-Khwārizmī's sidereal and al-Battānī's tropical longitudes.

L07-L10: the rows of Table 57a for the tenth, twentieth and thirtieth degree of each sign («Zeile X», «XXX° des Aquarius», «X° der Fische»): 9° 21′ for Pisces X, 9° 19′ for Aquarius XXX; to be compared with the table. N01: «facies» in italics, «Facies» (L07) upright.

L08 and N04: «Pisces», «Trigonometriske Tavler.», «Af Festskrift til» in italics; those of N04 look heavier than the other italics of the notes (the strokes measure the same, 5 px). Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Kh.», «Björnbo», «Burgess», «Thibaut», «Al-Chwarizmi», «Zeuthen»; italics also «Argument», «Breite,» and «Breite» (L02), «distantia definita», «Shaʿbān», «Ramaḍān», «Arin.» (L17; upright in L18), «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Panchasiddhāntikā», «Transl.».
The colon and the semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (9-13 px measured).
